hints: K can be as large as 10<sup>9</sup>, but rotating N times brings the array back to where it started. What does that tell you about K?
First reduce K = K % N. Then use the reversal trick: reverse the whole array, reverse the first K elements, reverse the remaining N − K. This rotates in place.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Move the array one step right, K times.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Copy each a[i] into a new array at position (i + K) % N.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Three reversals (whole, first K, rest) after reducing K modulo N.

explain: For 1 2 3 4 5 with K = 2: reversing everything gives 5 4 3 2 1, reversing the first two gives 4 5 3 2 1, reversing the last three gives 4 5 1 2 3. The last K elements need to move to the front, and the full reversal puts them there (backwards), so the two smaller reversals fix the order inside each block. Always take K % N first, otherwise huge K values break the indices; K % N = 0 leaves the array unchanged.
recognize: "Rotate by K steps" with large K → reduce K mod N, then the three-reversal trick (or index math).
python:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n, k = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
a = data[2:2 + n]
k %= n
print(" ".join(a[n - k:] + a[:n - k]))
